title: AI deepfake ad impersonating MrBeast on TikTok
system_purpose: Generative AI used to synthesize a real creator's face and voice for a fraudulent product-giveaway advertisement
decision_impact: Viewers could not tell the synthetic ad apart from genuine creator content, and the platform had to make a post-publication moderation call to remove it
verified_facts: TechCrunch reported a deepfake video/audio impersonation of creator MrBeast ran as a TikTok ad in October 2023 offering an iPhone 15 Pro for $2, and that TikTok removed the ad and states its policy requires synthetic media in ads to be disclosed.
reported_harm: Reported harm: viewer deception through an undisclosed synthetic impersonation of a real creator used to drive a scam offer; MrBeast publicly said the ad was unauthorized and warned platforms were not ready to handle AI deepfakes.
quantitative_evidence: The source confirms TikTok removed the ad but does not publish a verified count of views, clicks, or confirmed financial losses to viewers.
limitations: TechCrunch could not identify who created the deepfake ad; exact reach and any victim financial loss are not confirmed in this source, so downstream monetary-harm claims beyond this should be treated as unverified until a platform or regulator publishes figures.

title: Lehrman and Sage v. Lovo Inc. voice-cloning lawsuit
system_purpose: AI text-to-speech/voice-cloning platform ('Genny') used to generate synthetic voice tracks for narration and dubbing
decision_impact: Automated voice-cloning decided which submitted voice recordings became reusable synthetic voice products sold to platform customers for making content
affected_groups: voice actors;creators using cloned voices unknowingly;platform customers
verified_facts: CBS News reported that voice actors Paul Skye Lehrman and Linnea Sage filed a proposed class-action lawsuit in 2024 alleging Lovo cloned their voices from samples submitted in 2019-2020 for a stated internal-research purpose, then commercially reused the clones without further authorization; Lehrman said he discovered his cloned voice narrating an unrelated YouTube video and podcast he never recorded.
reported_harm: Reported harm: unauthorized commercial reuse of a person's cloned voice in content they never consented to appear in, plus alleged lost income; Sage reported losing an estimated 75% of her voiceover work that year, which she attributed in part to displacement by cloned-voice products.
quantitative_evidence: CBS News reports Sage's self-estimated 75% loss of voiceover work for the year as stated by the plaintiff; the article does not independently audit this figure or quantify how many other voice samples were affected.
limitations: This is a filed lawsuit with contested allegations, not a court finding of liability; Lovo did not respond to CBS News for comment when the article published; the 75% income-loss figure is the plaintiff's self-report, not an independently audited number, and this source does not report any final ruling on the merits.
